scenes.title: Three groups pass one problem along
scenes.narration: When a customer reports a problem, three groups of people pass it along until it is fixed.

steps.say: The customer writes in once, and never has to repeat the story.
A support agent owns the ticket from start to finish.
Engineering joins only when the agent finds a real bug.
And the customer hears back at every handover.

scenes.title: One owner, and help when it is a bug
scenes.narration: The customer sits outside. The support team owns the ticket, and engineering helps when the problem is a bug.

steps.say: The story starts with one customer who has a problem.
The customer writes to the help desk, and the message lands with one support agent.
That agent owns the ticket until it is resolved, whoever else helps.
The agent checks the help guides first, because most problems already have a known fix.
When the guides have no answer, the agent and the on-call engineer work on the problem together.

scenes.title: A wrong invoice, from report to fix
scenes.narration: Follow one ticket through the people who touch it.

steps.say: The customer reports a wrong invoice.
The agent checks the account first. The guides cover refunds, not this.
So the agent hands the ticket to the engineer, with every detail already gathered.
The engineer corrects the tax rate in the billing system.
And the billing system reissues the invoice.
The fix goes back to the agent, who tells the customer and sends the new invoice.

scenes.title: Each handover adds what the next person needs
scenes.narration: At each handover the ticket gains something the next person needs.

steps.say: The customer describes the problem once, in their own words.
The agent makes the problem happen again, and writes down the exact steps.
The engineer fixes the cause, so the next customer never sees the problem.
The agent confirms the fix with the customer and closes the ticket.

scenes.narration: A ticket like this spends most of its open time waiting on engineering.

steps.say: The clock starts when the customer writes in.
The customer hears back within an hour.
Three hours in, the agent hands the ticket to engineering.
Then seventeen hours pass while engineering finds and ships the fix.
The agent closes the ticket once the customer confirms, twenty two hours after it opened.
